paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Proverbs 28 keeps asking one question: who are you leaning on? The wicked run when nobody is chasing them, but "the righteous are as bold as a lion" (Proverbs 28:1). That kind of boldness doesn't come from a big bank account or a big title. It comes from a clear conscience and a God you can look in the eye.

Look at how the chapter treats the things people lean on instead. Money, power, flattery and a quick shortcut all promise a lot, and they all fall short. "Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a rich man whose ways are perverse" (Proverbs 28:6). And "He who trusts in himself is a fool, but one who walks in wisdom will be safe" (Proverbs 28:26). I once trusted myself with a tray in each hand and one on my head, and the floor was HAPPY about it.

So what do you do when you've already messed up? You don't hide it, baker. "He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy" (Proverbs 28:13). Turn toward God, say it plain, and let Him meet you with mercy. That's how a person ends up bold, and I can tell you from years of hiding in the back of a drawer, it beats hiding every time.
